- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast moderately, especially near end of horizon.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >70% spike) are common; apply downward correction of 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen tail end if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with trend; align forecast to sentiment-weighted moving average.
